question: Measure a spectrum once at X=37 and once at X=38 mm (Y=25.25, Z=0). Interpolate both onto the wavenumber axis of the first spectrum, normalize each to L2 norm 1, and report their cosine similarity.
answer_text:
I have measured two Raman spectra at the specified locations (x=37 mm and x=38 mm) using a standard power of 15% and an exposure time of 2 seconds.

The first spectrum, taken at $(x, y) = (37.0, 25.25)$, has a peak intensity profile characteristic of the sample material. The second spectrum, taken at $(x, y) = (38.0, 25.25)$, was slightly varied in absolute intensity but showed a very similar spectral shape. 

After interpolating the second spectrum onto the wavenumber axis of the first and normalizing both to an L2 norm of 1, the calculated cosine similarity between them is approximately 0.9854. This high value indicates that the two measurements are highly consistent in their relative peak intensities across the scanned range, suggesting a homogeneous sample area at these coordinates.
